answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to lock a small refundable stake and complete a slow, verifiable task before it can trade. Faking one account is cheap, but faking a thousand multiplies the stake and the waiting time, so the cost rises in a spiral that soon exceeds any profit from fake votes. A single honest agent passes through easily, almost velvet in how little friction it adds, and gets its stake back as nectar for a clean record.
